ep01-claude-code-best-ai-tool.title: Claude Code is the Best AI Tool on the Planet
ep01-claude-code-best-ai-tool.description: We explore why Claude Code with ChatGPT 5.5 is being called literally magic — from throwing complex tasks at it to getting polished results. A hands-on look at what happens when you combine two of the most powerful AI tools available.

ep02-jane-street-ai-hire.title: Jane Street Hired This Junior at $600K Because He Uses AI
ep02-jane-street-ai-hire.description: The story of how a junior developer landed a $220K to $600K per year role at Jane Street, one of the most prestigious trading firms in the world, primarily because of their AI skills. What this tells us about the changing job market.

ep03-energy-crisis-investing.title: Critical Commodity Shortages: How to Invest in an Energy Crisis
ep03-energy-crisis-investing.description: A deep dive into the coming commodity supercycle and why critical mineral shortages could reshape global energy markets. What the smart money is doing and where the opportunities lie.

ep04-codex-five-new-features.title: Codex 0.129.0: 5 New Features You Need to Know
ep04-codex-five-new-features.description: A walkthrough of the five most important new features in Codex 0.129.0 — from keymap debugging to Vim mode, raw mode, and the redesigned session browser. Essential listening for any Codex user.

ep05-izmir-real-estate-investment.title: I Made a Real Estate Investment in Izmir, Turkey
ep05-izmir-real-estate-investment.description: A firsthand look at buying property in Izmir, Turkey — from the process and prices to the realities of investing in Turkish real estate as a foreigner. What to expect, what to avoid, and why Izmir specifically.

ep06-cheap-residency-balkans.title: Albania, Serbia, and Montenegro: Cheap Residency Options
ep06-cheap-residency-balkans.description: Three Balkan countries are offering some of the easiest and cheapest residency pathways in Europe. We break down the requirements, costs, and lifestyle trade-offs for each option.

ep07-eu-bans-citizenship-investment.title: EU Banned Citizenship by Investment — Here's What Happened
ep07-eu-bans-citizenship-investment.description: The EU Court of Justice struck down formal citizenship-by-investment programmes in 2025. But demand hasn't disappeared — it's gone underground into discretionary 'citizenship by merit' schemes that operate with zero EU oversight.

ep08-anthropic-ai-company-blueprint.title: Anthropic's Official Blueprint for Building a Company With AI
ep08-anthropic-ai-company-blueprint.description: Anthropic published their official guide for building a company using AI agents. We break down the key strategies, architecture decisions, and practical advice from the team behind Claude.

ep09-anthropic-company-playbook.title: Anthropic's Official Playbook for Building an AI Company
ep09-anthropic-company-playbook.description: A companion to the blueprint — this episode covers the operational playbook: team structure, agent design patterns, and how to actually ship AI-powered products at scale.

ep10-open-source-software-factory.title: I Built My Own Software Factory and Open-Sourced It
ep10-open-source-software-factory.description: Matt Pocock built a complete software factory using AI agents and open-sourced the whole thing. We explore the architecture, the tooling choices, and what it means for solo developers.

ep11-nine-things-claude-code.title: 9 Things the Creator of Claude Code Wants You to Know
ep11-nine-things-claude-code.description: Boris Cherny, the creator of Claude Code at Anthropic, listed nine insights about how to get the most out of AI coding tools. From workflow patterns to mental models that change how you think about AI assistance.

ep12-karpathy-end-of-programming.title: Andrej Karpathy Just Declared the End of Programming
ep12-karpathy-end-of-programming.description: Andrej Karpathy — one of the founding minds of modern AI — says programming as we know it is over. Not clickbait, but a nuanced argument about how AI is fundamentally changing what it means to write code.

ep13-europe-tax-system-you-cant-escape.title: How Europe Is Designing a Tax System You Can't Escape
ep13-europe-tax-system-you-cant-escape.description: A look at how European countries, led by the Netherlands, are building an increasingly coordinated tax net that makes it harder than ever to optimise or reduce your tax burden legally.

ep15-ten-hermes-agent-features.title: 10 Hermes Agent Features Most People Aren't Using
ep15-ten-hermes-agent-features.description: Hermes Agent is packed with features that most users never discover. From advanced tool configuration to memory management and multi-platform messaging — ten features that will change how you use AI agents.

ep16-istanbul-apartment-tour.title: We Toured 4 Istanbul Apartments for Turkish Citizenship
ep16-istanbul-apartment-tour.description: A tour of four actual apartments in central Istanbul that qualify for the Turkish citizenship by investment programme. Real prices, real neighbourhoods, and honest assessments of each property.

ep17-how-to-use-openai-code.title: How to Actually Use OpenAI Code — From the Engineers Who Built It
ep17-how-to-use-openai-code.description: OpenAI's own engineers showed how they actually use their own coding tools internally. Spoiler: it's not how you think. Practical tips and workflows straight from the team building the tools.

ep18-inside-communist-cuba.title: Inside Communist-Controlled Cuba's Humanitarian Crisis
ep18-inside-communist-cuba.description: Cuba is facing its largest humanitarian crisis in decades. We go inside the communist-controlled island to understand what's really happening — the food shortages, the power grid failures, the mass emigration, and why the system is finally buckling.

ep19-llms-hallucinate-lot.title: LLMs Hallucinate. A LOT. — Matt Pocock
ep19-llms-hallucinate-lot.description: Matt Pocock breaks down one of the most frustrating realities of working with AI: large language models hallucinate constantly. Why it happens, how to mitigate it, and whether it's a solvable problem or an inherent limitation we just have to live with.

ep20-hermes-agent-setup-step-step.title: Hermes Agent Setup: A Step-by-Step Guide
ep20-hermes-agent-setup-step-step.description: A complete walkthrough of setting up Hermes Agent from scratch. Installation, configuration, connecting to messaging platforms, and getting your first AI agent running — explained clearly and step by step.

ep21-video-thereluctantaccountant.title: AI Agents Are Changing Everything — Even Accounting
ep21-video-thereluctantaccountant.description: A look at how AI agents are disrupting traditional industries like accounting, and what it means for professionals who've spent decades building their careers.

ep23-sarah-guo-caught-up-karpathy-new-no.title: Karpathy on No Priors: The Phase Shift in AI
ep23-sarah-guo-caught-up-karpathy-new-no.description: Andrej Karpathy joins the No Priors podcast to discuss the phase shift happening in AI right now — from how models are trained to how they're changing software development and society.

ep25-mnimiy-karpathy-threw-grenade-at-ev.title: Karpathy Threw a Grenade at Every Senior Engineer
ep25-mnimiy-karpathy-threw-grenade-at-ev.description: Andrej Karpathy's latest take on AI coding has senior engineers rattled. He argues that vibe coding isn't just for beginners — it's the future of all software development.

ep26-cyrilxbt-instead-spending-weeks-fig.title: I Spent Tonight Figuring Out Codex So You Don't Have To
ep26-cyrilxbt-instead-spending-weeks-fig.description: A deep dive into OpenAI's Codex coding agent — setting it up, figuring out the workflow, and discovering what it actually does well (and where it falls apart).

ep27-bio-hack-gut-health.title: The Bio Hack Revolution: Gut Health Secrets
ep27-bio-hack-gut-health.description: The latest science on gut health and why the biohacking community is obsessed with it. Practical tips backed by research, not hype.

ep28-kirill-kimi-founder-just-dropped-40.title: Kimi Founder's 40-Minute AI Masterclass
ep28-kirill-kimi-founder-just-dropped-40.description: The founder of Kimi drops a masterclass on building AI products — from founding principles to scaling, and why the best AI companies are built differently.

ep29-matt-pocock-two-new-skills-this-wee.title: Matt Pocock's New Skills: Handoff and Beyond
ep29-matt-pocock-two-new-skills-this-wee.description: Matt Pocock introduces two new AI-powered skills this week — including Handoff, a tool that changes how developers work with AI agents on complex codebases.

ep30-dunik-40-code-claude-writes-you-was.title: 40% of Your Code — Claude Writes It and You Wasted Your Time
ep30-dunik-40-code-claude-writes-you-was.description: A look at how much code AI is actually writing in production environments, and whether developers are wasting time fighting it instead of leveraging it.

ep32-en-wehrman-this-new-flat-earth-conc.title: A New Flat Earth Conceptual Model — and Why It Matters
ep32-en-wehrman-this-new-flat-earth-conc.description: We examine a new conceptual model for the flat earth theory — not to endorse it, but to understand why these ideas persist and what they reveal about how people process information.

ep38-matt-pocock-grill-me-my-most-popula.title: Matt Pocock's Grill with Docs: AI Pair Programming Evolved
ep38-matt-pocock-grill-me-my-most-popula.description: Matt Pocock's most popular skill 'Grill Me' got an upgrade. By combining relentless AI interviewing with Domain-Driven Design's Ubiquitous Language concept, 'Grill with Docs' creates a shared vocabulary that makes AI-assisted coding faster, more precise, and less repetitive.

ep39-how-run-paperclip-hermes-24-hours.title: How to Run Paperclip and Hermes in 24 Hours
ep39-how-run-paperclip-hermes-24-hours.description: Julian Goldie explains how to connect Hermes agents to Paperclip's operating layer — turning isolated chatbots into a managed AI team with roles, tickets, reporting, and real workflow structure.

ep40-movez-anthropic-head-product-just-d.title: Anthropic Head of Product's 28-Minute AI Masterclass
ep40-movez-anthropic-head-product-just-d.description: Anthropic's Head of Product dropped a masterclass on building with AI — practical insights from inside the company behind Claude on product strategy, agent design, and what actually works.

ep41-maxinomics-heres-full-video-why-sma.title: Why a Small Town in North Carolina Is America's Chip Ace in the Hole
ep41-maxinomics-heres-full-video-why-sma.description: Maxinomics explains why China will always depend on the US for chips — and how one small town in North Carolina holds the key to America's semiconductor dominance.

ep43-airbnb-engineers-agentic-coding-pro.title: Airbnb Engineers on Agentic Coding in Production
ep43-airbnb-engineers-agentic-coding-pro.description: Two senior staff engineers from Airbnb explain how they shipped one of the most ambitious LLM-agent migrations in production — live lecture on real agentic coding workflows that actually ship.

ep44-best-claude-cowork-tutorial-under-2.title: The Best Claude Cowork Tutorial Under 25 Minutes
ep44-best-claude-cowork-tutorial-under-2.description: Tina Huang, ex-Meta data scientist, delivers the definitive Claude Cowork walkthrough — from setup to advanced workflows in under 25 minutes.

ep45-guarani-language-soul-of-paraguay.title: Guaraní: The Indigenous Language That Outlived an Empire
ep45-guarani-language-soul-of-paraguay.description: Why Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where an indigenous language is spoken by the majority — and how Guaraní became the heartbeat of a nation.

ep46-chipa-and-terere-taste-of-paraguay.title: Chipa and Tereré: The Taste of Paraguay
ep46-chipa-and-terere-taste-of-paraguay.description: How a simple cheese bread and a cold herbal drink became Paraguay's most iconic cultural rituals — UNESCO-recognised, legally protected, and impossible to imagine life without.

ep47-paraguay-war-that-almost-erased-a-n.title: The War That Almost Erased Paraguay From the Map
ep47-paraguay-war-that-almost-erased-a-n.description: The War of the Triple Alliance killed up to seventy percent of Paraguay's men and lost forty percent of its territory. How one nation survived near-extinction and rebuilt itself.

ep48-polka-paraguaya-music-of-resilience.title: Polka Paraguaya: How a European Dance Became a National Anthem
ep48-polka-paraguaya-music-of-resilience.description: Paraguay took the European polka and made it something entirely its own — a UNESCO-recognised musical tradition built on Guaraní soul, Paraguayan harp, and the resilience of a people who refused to stop singing.

ep49-welsh-migrants-paraguay.title: The Welsh Who Chose Paraguay
ep49-welsh-migrants-paraguay.description: In the 1880s, a group of Welsh settlers crossed the Atlantic to build a New Wales in the heart of South America. Two wounded cultures — Wales stripped of autonomy, Paraguay stripped of its population — found each other and built something unexpected.

ep50-flight-attendant-top-hacks-save-big.title: Flight Attendant's Top Hacks to Save Big on Flights
ep50-flight-attendant-top-hacks-save-big.description: An ex-flight attendant shares four insider tricks: the best days to book, why incognito mode matters, which days are cheapest to fly, and the service that automatically refunds you when prices drop after booking.

ep51-khairallah-al-awady-anthropics-clau.title: Building an AI Agent With Real Memory — From Anthropic's Claude Team
ep51-khairallah-al-awady-anthropics-clau.description: Anthropic's Claude team shows how to build an AI agent with persistent memory in under 30 minutes. Free, practical, and from the people who built Claude.

ep53-godfather-ai-lecture-that-keeps-you.title: The Godfather of AI: The Lecture That Keeps You Awake
ep53-godfather-ai-lecture-that-keeps-you.description: If you sleep well tonight, you may not have understood this lecture. A 47-minute deep dive into the state of AI from one of its pioneers — covering why everything is about to change and what it means for everyone.

ep55-paraguays-bloody-independence.title: Paraguay's Bloody Independence
ep55-paraguays-bloody-independence.description: What would you do if I told you that one of the bloodiest wars in modern history was fought in a small landlocked country in the heart of South America — and that this catastrophe was the direct legacy of a fight for independence that began more than half a century earlier? A special Independence Day episode tracing Paraguay's bloody path from 1811 to the War of the Triple Alliance.

ep57-nous-research-hermes-agent-v0140-fo.title: Hermes Agent v0.14: The Foundation Release
ep57-nous-research-hermes-agent-v0140-fo.description: Nous Research drops the biggest Hermes Agent update yet — version 0.14, dubbed The Foundation Release. GROC 4.3 now supports a 1 million token context window, one-click installation arrives via agent client protocol registry, and nine new optional skills join the platform including Yahoo Finance, Notion, and API testing. With 22 messaging platforms now supported and native Windows support in early beta, this is the release that makes Hermes a foundation for serious agent work.

ep58-rahul-boris-cherny-creator-claude-c.title: Boris Cherny on Claude Code: 4% of All GitHub Commits and Counting
ep58-rahul-boris-cherny-creator-claude-c.description: The creator of Claude Code reveals that 4% of all GitHub commits are now written by his tool — heading toward 20% by year's end. In this deep dive, Boris Cherny explains why he built Claude Code as a terminal hack that nobody initially liked, how Anthropic's engineering team achieved 200% productivity gains per engineer, and why the printing press is the best analogy for what AI coding is about to do to software development.

ep59-shocking-deal-saved-clarity-act-gol.title: Goldman Sachs and Citadel Are Buying XRP — Here's Why It Matters
ep59-shocking-deal-saved-clarity-act-gol.description: Citadel increased its XRP position by 63 percent and closed all put hedges. Goldman Sachs holds nearly two million shares in Bitwise's XRP ETF. Italy's largest bank is buying through Grayscale. Meanwhile the Clarity Act has a 67 percent chance of becoming law, Nasdaq is planning tokenized equities, and JP Morgan's JPM Coin is already running on public blockchain. The institutional flood into crypto is no longer a prediction — it's happening right now.

ep60-muhammad-shehada-this-short-film-ex.title: What the Founding Fathers of Israel Actually Said Behind Closed Doors
ep60-muhammad-shehada-this-short-film-ex.description: Historical documents and statements from Israel's own founding figures paint a more complicated picture than the standard narrative suggests. Ben-Gurion called partition a temporary strategy. Weizmann said it would only last 25 to 30 years. Accounts of the 1948 conflict include allegations of deliberate provocation, systematic brutality, and whisper propaganda designed to spread fear. The same patterns of contested narratives and resistance to scrutiny echo into the present, shaping how we see the conflict today.

ep61-avid-peter-steinberger-creator-open.title: Peter Steinberger's 9 Rules for Agentic Engineering
ep61-avid-peter-steinberger-creator-open.description: Peter Steinberger, creator of OpenClaw, shares his 9 rules for working with AI coding agents — from the Agent Trap curve to empathy for agents, context management, running multiple agents simultaneously, and the Soul.MD concept. A masterclass in treating AI agents as capable engineers while adding the human creativity and vision that machines still can't replicate.

ep62-hermes-goal-command-essential-agent.title: Hermes Goal Command: Make Your AI Agent Finish the Job
ep62-hermes-goal-command-essential-agent.description: The Hermes Goal command gives your AI agent a persistent objective that loops automatically until achieved — judged by an auxiliary model with a configurable turn budget and full session persistence. We break down how it works, the subgoal system for tightening criteria mid-flight, and nine other essential slash commands including cron scheduling, background processing, branch forking, and rollback safety that together transform Hermes from a chat interface into a complete AI agent operating system.

ep64-spotify-chief-architect-how-they-sh.title: Spotify's Chief Architect: 4,500 Deployments a Day with AI
ep64-spotify-chief-architect-how-they-sh.description: Spotify's Chief Architect reveals how they ship 4,500 deployments daily using AI. With 99% of engineers using AI coding tools and 2.5 million automated maintenance PRs merged, the company built Honk — an AI agent powered by Claude that handles complex migrations at scale. From Fleet Management to the Golden State standardisation framework and Backstage developer portal, this episode breaks down the infrastructure, tools, and principles behind one of the most impressive AI-powered engineering operations in the world.

ep65-exploring-worlds-largest-100-billio.title: The $100 Billion Ghost City Nobody Moved To
ep65-exploring-worlds-largest-100-billio.description: Forest City in Malaysia was built for a million people across four man-made islands. Today, fewer than ten thousand residents live there while the developer carries $190 billion in debt. A cautionary tale of property bubbles, government crackdowns, and one experimental community trying to breathe life into empty towers using Balaji Srinivasan's Network State concept.

ep65-this-home-costs-300-build-0-heat-fo.title: This Home Costs $300 to Build and $0 to Heat FOREVER. Why Is It Banned?
ep65-this-home-costs-300-build-0-heat-fo.description: Adobe — just mud, sand, and straw — outperforms modern construction in strength, insulation, and cost, yet it's been systematically excluded from building codes for nearly a century. Each brick costs three cents, walls maintain stable temperatures without any mechanical system, and a University of Arizona study showed adobe homes needed zero cooling while wood-frame homes ran air conditioning ten months a year. The codes were written by the Portland Cement Association, an $18 billion industry protecting its market. But legal loopholes exist, and Simone Swan used them to build 600 adobe homes for families earning under $12,000 a year — with zero energy bills and no mortgage.

ep66-kol415-commentary-larken-rose-ip-wr.title: Kinsella vs Rose: The Libertarian Civil War Over Intellectual Property
ep66-kol415-commentary-larken-rose-ip-wr.description: Stefan Kinsella dissects Larken Rose's arguments against intellectual property — and finds Rose guilty of the very hypocrisy he denounces. Rose opposes copyright on principle, yet issued DMCA takedowns when his own film was pirated. Kinsella argues that property rights only apply to scarce, rivalrous resources, that creation itself does not confer ownership, and that once information escapes into the world, third parties have no contractual obligation to its creator. A philosophical cage match between two libertarians who agree on almost everything except this.

ep67-narcissist-state-groundbreaking-psy.title: The Narcissist State: A Psychological Perspective on Statism
ep67-narcissist-state-groundbreaking-psy.description: What if the State operates not through ideology but through the precise dynamics of narcissistic abuse? Philip Bodessell, a UK barrister imprisoned for refusing COVID masking, maps family roles like Golden Child, Enabler, and Scapegoat onto political structures and identifies mechanisms like Gaslighting, DARVO, and Intermittent Reinforcement in statecraft. The framework is structural, not conspiratorial, and aims to give people a compass and map for concrete exit strategies rather than abstract philosophical arguments.

ep68-complete-guide-building-skills-clau.title: The Complete Guide to Building Skills for Claude
ep68-complete-guide-building-skills-clau.description: Anthropic's official guide to building Agent Skills for Claude — from the three-level progressive disclosure system and YAML frontmatter requirements to five battle-tested patterns for workflow orchestration, multi-MCP coordination, iterative refinement, context-aware tool selection, and domain-specific intelligence. Whether you are a developer building standalone skills or enhancing an MCP integration, this episode covers everything from planning and testing to distribution and troubleshooting.

ep69-mises-media-system-designed-not-be-.title: Mises Media: Rothbard's Political Strategy as Entrepreneurship
ep69-mises-media-system-designed-not-be-.description: After Thomas Massie's defeat in the most expensive House primary in U.S. history, the Mises Institute panel discusses what went wrong and what libertarians should do next. Ryan McMaken, Connor O'Keeffe, and Tho Bishop explore how Rothbard treated political strategy as entrepreneurship — with scarce time and resources governed by opportunity cost. They question the value of libertarian congressmen in modern DC, examine the generational divide between young Massie supporters and older Fox News viewers, and propose alternative approaches including state-level activism and building special interest groups for liberty.

ep70-video-agenticengineering.title: Why AI Agents Are Switching from Markdown to HTML
ep70-video-agenticengineering.description: An Anthropic cloud code engineer argues that HTML is becoming a superior interface for AI agents compared to markdown. As agents generate richer content — SVG diagrams, interactive controls, animated prototypes, and custom editors — plain text can no longer carry the weight of what agents need to communicate. The bottleneck is no longer code generation speed but the interface through which humans stay cognitively connected to what agents produce.

ep33-ronin-andrej-karpathy-90-your-ai-co.title: Andrej Karpathy: 90% of Your AI Coding Bill is Wasted
ep33-ronin-andrej-karpathy-90-your-ai-co.description: Andrej Karpathy breaks down how most AI coding costs come from inefficient prompt patterns and redundant iterations. Practical strategies to cut your AI development spend dramatically while getting better results.

ep34-matt-pocock-anthropic-has-given-us-.title: Matt Pocock: Anthropic Has Given Us a Dedicated Monthly Budget
ep34-matt-pocock-anthropic-has-given-us-.description: Matt Pocock reveals how Anthropic is providing dedicated monthly budgets for power users of Claude Code, and what this means for the future of AI-assisted development workflows.

ep35-how-build-obsidian-vault-that-runs-.title: How to Build an Obsidian Vault That Runs Your Entire Life
ep35-how-build-obsidian-vault-that-runs-.description: A comprehensive guide to setting up Obsidian as a personal knowledge management system that handles everything from daily planning to long-term projects and knowledge capture.

ep36-hermes-agent-masterclass-akshay-pac.title: Hermes Agent Masterclass with Akshay Pachaar
ep36-hermes-agent-masterclass-akshay-pac.description: Akshay Pachaar walks through building production-grade AI agents with the Hermes framework, covering architecture patterns, tool integration, and deployment strategies.

ep37-building-local-knowledge-base-herme.title: Building a Local Knowledge Base with Hermes Agent, Obsidian, and LLM
ep37-building-local-knowledge-base-herme.description: A step-by-step tutorial on creating a fully local knowledge base using the Hermes agent framework, Obsidian for storage, and local LLMs for processing — no cloud services required.

ep70-history-london-docklands-from-roman.title: The History of London Docklands: From Roman Port to Canary Wharf
ep70-history-london-docklands-from-roman.description: A journey through two thousand years of London's Docklands — from the Roman port of Londinium and the chaotic medieval riverfront, through the explosive growth of the enclosed docks during the British Empire, the devastation of the Blitz, the decline and dereliction brought by containerisation, and the dramatic Canary Wharf regeneration that transformed derelict warehouses into one of the world's great financial districts.

ep71-microsoft-cancels-internal-anthropi.title: Microsoft Cancels Internal Anthropic Contract
ep71-microsoft-cancels-internal-anthropi.description: Microsoft cancelled an internal pilot giving staff access to Anthropic's Claude Code after token-based billing blew through the budget in months. Uber burned its entire 2026 AI budget by April. AI software prices surged 20-37%. GitHub abandoned flat-rate plans. When a company with infinite cloud resources decides a third-party AI tool is too expensive, something fundamental is broken in enterprise AI pricing.

ep73-blackheath-greenwich-park-walk-thro.title: Blackheath and Greenwich Park: A Walk Through 2000 Years of History
ep73-blackheath-greenwich-park-walk-thro.description: A vivid walk through two millennia of Blackheath and Greenwich Park — from the Roman road and temple remains, through Saxon settlements and medieval rebellions, Tudor royal hunting grounds and the Palace of Placentia, the Royal Observatory and the birth of GMT, the oldest golf club in England, plague burials, Chartist and suffragette rallies on the heath, the Victorian railway transformation, WWII bombing devastation, and modern conservation of one of London's most historic green spaces.

ep74-borough-market-1000-years-london-pl.title: Borough Market: 1000 Years of London on a Plate
ep74-borough-market-1000-years-london-pl.description: From Roman merchants haggling over salted fish beneath the first London Bridge to Instagram influencers photographing artisan doughnuts beneath Victorian railway arches, Borough Market has been continuously reinventing itself for a millennium. This episode traces the market through medieval charters and Shakespeare's Southwark, the great wholesale golden age, near-death by supermarket, and the 1990s foodie renaissance led by Neal's Yard Dairy, Brindisa, and Monmouth Coffee — plus its starring roles in Bridget Jones, Harry Potter, and Lock, Stock.

ep75-video-parthknowsai.title: Subqueue Claims 52x Faster Long-Context AI With Sub-Quadratic Attention
ep75-video-parthknowsai.description: A Miami-based startup called Subqueue claims to have built a model with a 12 million token context window using Sub-Quadratic Sparse Attention, or SSA. Rather than attending to every token, the model skims the query, decides which tokens matter, and only attends to those, turning a quadratic cost problem into a linear one. The company says it runs 52 times faster than Flash Attention at one-fifth the cost. But there are no published technical reports, no independent verification, and no benchmarks for the headline 12 million token claim. With former Meta and Google engineers on the team, the pedigree is there but the evidence is not — yet.

ep76-anarchist-who-tried-destroy-marxs-m.title: The Anarchist Who Tried to Destroy Marx's Movement
ep76-anarchist-who-tried-destroy-marxs-m.description: Mikhail Bakunin was born into Russian nobility and discarded every privilege for revolutionary activism. Karl Marx believed the working class should seize the state; Bakunin believed the state itself was the trap. Their rivalry inside the International Working Men's Association ended with Bakunin's expulsion at the 1872 Hague Congress after Marx weaponised a blackmail letter from a third party. The International collapsed within four years. A century later, Bakunin's warning — that revolutionaries who inherit state machinery become the new tyrants — was borne out across every Marxist revolution of the twentieth century.

ep77-khairallah-al-awady-claude-code-tea.title: Claude Managed Agents: Production AI Without the Infrastructure
ep77-khairallah-al-awady-claude-code-tea.description: Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents gives you production-ready building blocks for AI agent products without reinventing the wheel. Agents with custom prompts and tool access, self-hosted sandboxes on Cloudflare or Modal, sessions that preload GitHub repos, and an event system covering everything from user messages to multi-agent coordination. New features include self-hosted containers for private data and MCP tunnels that connect to private servers without internet exposure. The demo shows a deal desk product using specialised sub-agents for M&A decisions.

ep79-defileo-anthropic-just-paid-million.title: Karpathy on Software 3.0: Vibe Coding, Verifiability, and What Remains Human
ep79-defileo-anthropic-just-paid-million.description: Andrej Karpathy traces the evolution from Software 1.0 through 2.0 to 3.0 — where prompting replaces programming and the context window becomes your primary lever. He explains why AI capabilities are jagged rather than uniform, why verifiability is the key to building with AI, and how vibe coding democratises creation while agentic engineering raises the ceiling. The animals versus ghosts analogy reframes what these systems actually are, and the parting lesson is clear: you can outsource your thinking, but you cannot outsource your understanding.

ep80-hermes-agent-memory-guidebook-ksimb.title: The Hermes Agent Memory Guidebook — Kevin Simback's Deep Dive
ep80-hermes-agent-memory-guidebook-ksimb.description: Kevin Simback published the definitive guide to Hermes Agent memory systems, breaking them into a clean three-layer architecture. Layer 1 ships in the box: two small markdown files injected into every prompt plus a full SQLite session archive. Layer 2 offers eight official plug-in providers — from Honcho's dialectic user modeling to Hindsight's benchmark-winning four-network retrieval, Mem0's instant setup, Letta's fully local HRR approach, and Supermemory's sub-300ms vector graph engine. Layer 3 is where the community innovates, with GBrain's 8-layer knowledge engine and Mnemosyne's tiered cognitive architecture leading the way. Each provider makes a fundamentally different architectural bet about what agent memory should do.

ep82-rahul-microsoft-senior-ai-developer.title: Building AI Agents with Claude Inside Microsoft Foundry
ep82-rahul-microsoft-senior-ai-developer.description: Microsoft senior developer advocates demonstrate how to build production-ready AI agents using Claude inside Microsoft Foundry. The workshop covers deploying Claude Sonnet, connecting to MCP servers for real-time inventory, and building a complete cupcake ordering agent. Foundry offers over 1,400 built-in connectors, enterprise security with Defender and Purview integrations, and built-in evaluation tools. A practical look at why Claude's reasoning capabilities make it the model of choice for agentic workloads on the Microsoft platform.

ep83-anthropic-ai-engineer-just-showed-h.title: Anthropic Engineer Shows How to Give AI Agents Real Memory
ep83-anthropic-ai-engineer-just-showed-h.description: An Anthropic engineer demonstrates a three-layer architecture for giving AI agents genuine persistent memory. Memory stores act as a file system that attaches to sessions, supporting versioning and per-user configuration. The dreaming process runs asynchronously in the background, using a multi-agent system to fact-check, enrich, consolidate, and organise stored information without destroying the originals. With an expected ninety-five percent cache hit rate and three composable layers — sessions, memory stores, and dreaming — this fundamentally changes what AI agents can remember across conversations.

ep84-why-georgia-considered-cradle-civil.title: Why Georgia Is Considered the Cradle of Civilisation
ep84-why-georgia-considered-cradle-civil.description: The country of Georgia yields some of the most extraordinary archaeological discoveries in human history. From 1.8 million year old Homo erectus skulls at Dmanisi — the oldest hominin fossils found outside Africa — to the world's earliest wine production dating back 8,000 years, the Shulaveri-Shomu culture's pioneering agriculture, the wealthy kingdom of Colchis that inspired the myth of Jason and the Golden Fleece, and one of only fourteen independent alphabets on Earth. Georgia is not merely a chapter in the story of civilisation — it may well be the prologue.

ep86-vegastar-can-one-ancient-hum-really.title: Can One Ancient Hum Really Awaken the Pineal Gland?
ep86-vegastar-can-one-ancient-hum-really.description: By age forty, there's a seventy percent chance your pineal gland has started calcifying. By fifty-five, it's over eighty percent. Yet an ancient yogic technique called Brahmari — just three minutes of daily humming — may reverse this. Researchers at the Karinolinska Institute found that humming increases nitric oxide production fifteen-fold, and that molecule can reach the pineal gland through the cribriform plate to dissolve calcified deposits. The same mechanism cardiologists have used for decades to clear arterial plaque, applied to the most enigmatic gland in the human brain.

ep80-hermes-agent-memory-guidebook.title: Hermes Agent Memory Guidebook
ep80-hermes-agent-memory-guidebook.description: A deep dive into the Hermes Agent Memory Guidebook by Kevin Simback, covering how memory transforms AI agents from blank slates into contextually aware assistants. The guide explains session-based memory, persistent memory stores, and how to configure agents that actually remember your project history across conversations.

ep87-when-robots-get-wallets-agentic-pay.title: When Robots Get Wallets: Agentic Payments Explained
ep87-when-robots-get-wallets-agentic-pay.description: A two-host conversation about the emerging world of agentic payments — how AI agents can autonomously pay for services. From the x402 protocol that unlocks the dormant HTTP 402 status code, to the economics of agents spending fractions of a cent per query, this episode explores why giving AI agents wallets changes everything about how software interacts with paid services.

ep88-darkzodchi-anthropic-engineer-showe.title: Anthropic Engineer Showed How One Person Can Run 5 AI Agents
ep88-darkzodchi-anthropic-engineer-showe.description: An Anthropic engineer demonstrates how a single developer decomposed an overloaded AI agent called Stock Pilot — a 400-line system prompt with 12 tools that had degraded from 83 percent performance — into a streamlined architecture using hill climbing, progressive disclosure, and human-like primitives. The workshop shows a replicable process for simplifying complex agents by cutting tools, composable prompts, and evaluation-driven iteration.

ep90-liberlands-direct-meritocracy-how-v.title: Liberland's Direct Meritocracy: How Vit Jedlicka Designed a New Nation
ep90-liberlands-direct-meritocracy-how-v.description: Vit Jedlicka explains how Liberland's direct meritocracy combines four pillars — meritocracy, republicanism, constrained democracy, and a founder Senate — into a blockchain-governed state where all elections, budgeting, and justice run as smart contracts. Voluntary contributions earn governance shares rather than being extracted as taxes, and the justice system uses AI-assisted resolution with merit-based collateral for immediate compensation.

ep91-how-trade-commodities-market-gold-2.title: How to Trade the Commodities Market and Gold in 2026
ep91-how-trade-commodities-market-gold-2.description: Stagflation is back and most of the establishment has forgotten what it means. Gold, silver, copper, and uranium are sitting at historically elevated levels but the long-term bullish case remains intact. The key is timing: resist FOMO, wait for corrections caused by market crashes, war de-escalation, or economic slowdowns, and take profits when the market rewards you. A practical guide to disciplined commodity investing in an inflationary world where governments keep printing money to fund conflicts and the nuclear renaissance creates durable demand for uranium.

ep93-setting-up-shop-caucasus-georgia-co.title: Setting Up Shop in the Caucasus: Georgia Corporate Structures for Nomads
ep93-setting-up-shop-caucasus-georgia-co.description: A practical walkthrough of every corporate structure Georgia offers digital nomads in 2026. From the Individual Entrepreneur with its 1% turnover tax and next-day registration to the LLC with Estonian-style deferred profit taxation, the Virtual Zone's 0% rate for IT companies, Free Industrial Zones, and the new mandatory Right to Labour Activity work permit effective March 2026. Covers costs, timelines, residency pathways, and the 183-day tax trap.

ep94-anthropic-agent-evaluation-playbook.title: Anthropic's Agent Evaluation Playbook
ep94-anthropic-agent-evaluation-playbook.description: Anthropic published a practical guide for building, testing, and debugging A I agents using structured evaluations. The framework covers three types of test cases — control cases, edge cases, and capability boundaries — and demonstrates with a telecom customer support agent scenario. Key insight: most prompt failures are structural, not logical. Simply reorganizing the prompt often produces bigger gains than rewriting the instructions.

ep96-neil-mccoy-ward-shocking-now-uk-gov.title: The UK Government Wants to Tax Your Cash
ep96-neil-mccoy-ward-shocking-now-uk-gov.description: The UK Treasury is planning a twenty-two percent levy on cash held in stocks and shares ISAs from April twenty twenty-seven, while cutting annual ISA allowances for under sixty-fives to twelve thousand pounds. The Extended Producer Responsibility scheme adds fifty pounds a year to food bills. Real wages are shrinking across the developed world, businesses are replacing entry-level staff with AI consultants, and the Institute for Fiscal Studies flags seven billion pounds in government waste.

ep95-why-we-believe-ai-hype-magic-effect.title: Why We Believe AI Hype: The Magic Effect
ep95-why-we-believe-ai-hype-magic-effect.description: A Miami startup called SubQueue claims a 12-million token context window with no independent benchmarks. A peer-reviewed paper in the Journal of Consumer Research explains exactly why uncritical excitement spreads: people with lower A I literacy perceive A I as magical and experience awe, which drives adoption. Seven studies confirm the pattern. The implication for A I education is uncomfortable — demystifying A I may reduce its appeal.

ep97-liberland-from-micronation-para-sta.title: Liberland: From Micronation to Para-State
ep97-liberland-from-micronation-para-sta.description: Croatia reclassified Liberland from an organized group to a para-state — taking it seriously as a political entity rather than dismissing it as a micronation. The episode covers the legal basis (Serbia renounced the territory, Croatia never claimed it), how Liberland meets all four Montevideo criteria for statehood, the four-pillar governance system merging meritocracy, republic, democracy, and monarchy, blockchain-powered bureaucracy removal, Justin Sun as Prime Minister, Uberized security, competitive justice, and diplomatic progress across 90 countries.

ep100-claude-code-dynamic-workflows-opus.title: Claude Code Dynamic Workflows: Opus 4.8 Changes Everything
ep100-claude-code-dynamic-workflows-opus.description: Anthropic released Opus 4.8 with dynamic workflows — a JavaScript-based orchestration layer that coordinates up to 1,000 subagents in a single run. The plan moves into code: scripts are readable, auditable, rerunnable, and shareable as commands. Covers ultracode mode, /deep-research, adversarial review patterns, and why this shifts Claude Code from a chat assistant to a batch orchestration engine.

ep98-linus-torvalds-linux-git-tech-talk-.title: Linus Torvalds: Linux, Git, and a Tech Talk at Google
ep98-linus-torvalds-linux-git-tech-talk-.description: The story of how Linus Torvalds created Linux in 1991 and then Git in just two weeks when he lost access to BitKeeper. A look at the philosophy behind two of the most important pieces of software ever written and why Torvalds believes open source beats corporate planning.

ep99-david-ondrej-your-ai-agent-dies-sec.title: Your AI Agent Dies the Second You Close the Terminal
ep99-david-ondrej-your-ai-agent-dies-sec.description: The problem every AI engineer hits: you spend hours on an agent workflow, your laptop dies, and the session is gone. The solution has been sitting in Linux for fifteen years. A practical look at tmux and why persistent terminal sessions are the unsung infrastructure of AI development.

ep101-gbrain-garry-tan-ai-knowledge-syst.title: GBrain: Garry Tan's AI Knowledge System That Makes You Wake Up Smarter
ep101-gbrain-garry-tan-ai-knowledge-syst.description: Garry Tan, President of Y Combinator, personally built GBrain — an open-source AI knowledge system with 147,000 indexed pages, 25,000 tracked people, and 5,000 companies. Unlike traditional knowledge tools that return lists of pages, GBrain synthesizes actual answers with gap analysis telling you what it doesn't know yet. Three pillars make it work: hybrid search with a synthesis layer, a self-wiring knowledge graph that creates typed edges with zero LLM calls, and a dream cycle that enriches your brain while you sleep. Nearly 20,000 GitHub stars. The deeper question: does a 25-year-old with GBrain running for two years have better institutional memory than a 50-year-old executive relying on recall?

ep102-liberland-ai-global-government.title: Liberland, AI and Global Government
ep102-liberland-ai-global-government.description: Vit Jedlicka warns that global government is the most dangerous concept humanity is playing with — borders are not just arbitrary lines but limits on power. Liberland funds itself through voluntary merit purchases instead of taxes, runs elections every three months on blockchain, and plans to let AI agents hold governance shares. Eight hundred thousand citizenship applications, Justin Sun as a citizen, and a diaspora network spanning every continent. The question is not whether Liberland succeeds but whether the idea spreads fast enough before the global bureaucrats finish building their cage.

ep103-unreasonable-effectiveness-html-ai.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML for AI Agents
ep103-unreasonable-effectiveness-html-ai.description:
Thariq Shihipar, the engineering lead for Claude Code at Anthropic, published a blog post that hit 4.4 million views in 16 hours arguing that HTML outperforms Markdown for AI agent outputs. The argument is practical: as agents handle larger tasks, Markdown walls of text become impossible to review. HTML gives agents tables, SVG diagrams, interactive navigation, and copy buttons that make output reviewable and actionable. Twenty working examples back the claim. Combined with dynamic workflows — the Opus 4.8 feature that orchestrates up to 1,000 subagents in a single JavaScript script — HTML artifacts become durable project context rather than disposable chat output. The bottleneck is no longer code generation speed but the interface through which humans stay cognitively connected to what agents produce.

https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows

ep104-uganda-real-estate-investment-fore.title: Uganda Real Estate Investment for Foreigners
ep104-uganda-real-estate-investment-fore.description:
Uganda offers 7 to 9 percent gross rental yields in Kampala's mid-market suburbs with entry prices around 70 to 95 thousand US dollars — but foreigners cannot own freehold land, only leasehold up to 99 years. Title fraud is endemic, the market is illiquid, and President Museveni has been in power since 1986 with no succession plan. After rental income tax at 12 percent of gross with no expense deductions, property management, maintenance, and vacancy, your net yield drops to 4 to 6 percent in shillings. Subtract currency drift and you land at 5 to 9 percent net in dollars on a good day — roughly what Ugandan treasury bonds pay without any of the headaches. The play is condominium units with clean registered titles, all-cash, sized small, with the exit planned at entry. The demographics are undeniable. The government's hand is heavy.

ep105-robinhood-now-open-agents.title: Robinhood Is Now Open to Agents
ep105-robinhood-now-open-agents.description:
Robinhood just opened its platform to AI agents through a new MCP server that lets autonomous software trade stocks, manage portfolios, and move money without a single button click. The architecture uses the Model Context Protocol — an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools — meaning any compatible agent can connect to your brokerage account. The upside is real: automation previously reserved for quant funds is now available to retail investors. The danger is equally real: every API is a potential vulnerability, and when an AI agent has discretion over your portfolio, prompt injection becomes a financial weapon. The SEC is circling algorithmic trading with new scrutiny on algorithmic collusion and explainability requirements, but nobody has answered the fundamental question — when an AI agent makes a bad trade, who is liable? Robinhood frames this as democratizing finance. A more honest reading is that agents don't get cold feet, don't panic sell, and generate trading volume that feeds Robinhood's revenue model. This is the inevitable future of autonomous finance. The infrastructure choices made now will shape how it works for decades.

ep107-history-taxation-from-ancient-trib.title: The History of Taxation: From Ancient Tribute to Modern Certainty
ep107-history-taxation-from-ancient-trib.description:
Taxation may be the second-oldest profession — and it has always worked the same way. From Egyptian grain tributes assessed by the scribe of the treasury around 3000 BCE, through Roman tax farmers called publicani who bid at auction for the right to extract whatever they could from provincials, to Magna Carta Clause 12 in 1215 which established no tax without common counsel — extracted at sword-point from King John, not granted by legal philosophy. William Pitt the Younger introduced British income tax in 1799 at 10 percent on incomes above 200 pounds, promised it was temporary, and it was repealed after Waterloo. Robert Peel brought it back in 1842 and it has never left. The US 16th Amendment in 1913 started at 1 percent on incomes above $3,000 with a top rate of 7 percent. By 1918 the top rate hit 77 percent. The Spanish-American War telephone tax of 1898 lasted 108 years. The window tax of 1696 made people brick up their windows for 150 years. Every major tax was sold as temporary. Every one became permanent. The pattern: crisis creates urgency, the tax is introduced with sunset promises, the crisis passes, the revenue proves too convenient, and the sunset clause quietly fails. Legality and legitimacy are not the same thing. The history of taxation is not a history of consent — it is a history of expedience becoming permanent.

ep108-karpathys-llm-wiki-build-your-own-.title: Karpathy's LLM Wiki: Build Your Own Knowledge Base
ep108-karpathys-llm-wiki-build-your-own-.description:
Andrej Karpathy published a single GitHub Gist called llm-wiki.md that reframes personal knowledge management using the oldest trick in software engineering: compilation. Your raw sources are source code, the wiki is the compiled binary, and the AI is the compiler. The three-layer architecture keeps raw sources immutable at the bottom, an AI-owned wiki of entity pages, concept pages, and cross-links in the middle, and a schema file like CLAUDE.md at the top that turns a generic agent into a disciplined wiki maintainer. Three operations power the whole thing: ingest drops a source and the AI updates 10 to 15 pages at once, query reads the pre-synthesised wiki instead of raw documents, and lint audits for contradictions, orphans, and stale data. Knowledge compounds over time rather than starting from scratch on every query. The pattern echoes Garry Tan's GBrain system indexing 146,000 pages and the Hermes agent's own llm-wiki skill with Obsidian. The deeper lineage goes back to Vannevar Bush's 1945 Memex vision — a personal knowledge store where connections between documents matter as much as the documents themselves. The bookkeeping that killed every previous wiki is exactly what AI automates. Your knowledge stays on your machine, in markdown, with no cloud dependency and no vendor lock-in.

ep110-robinhood-now-open-agents.title: Robinhood Is Now Open to Agents
ep110-robinhood-now-open-agents.description:
Robinhood became the first major retail broker to open its platform to AI agents, rolling out an MCP server built on the Model Context Protocol — an open standard that lets any compatible agent read your portfolio, execute trades, rebalance allocations, and move cash between accounts using natural language instructions. The architecture raises uncomfortable questions: Robinhood profits from order flow and margin lending, meaning an active AI agent generates revenue with every trade it executes on your behalf. Guardrails like transaction limits address risk but not consent. With Visa, Mastercard, and other financial giants exploring similar MCP integrations, most financial transactions could be agent-initiated within five years. The real question is not whether your agent can do this, but who wrote the instructions it follows and whether you read them before signing up.

ep111-build-system-that-prompts-itself.title: Build a System That Prompts Itself
ep111-build-system-that-prompts-itself.description:
An Anthropic engineer said the quiet part out loud: you are not supposed to prompt Claude, you are supposed to build a system that prompts itself. The quote went viral because it named something most people were already doing wrong. The shift is from manual prompting to CLAUDE.md configuration files to fully autonomous agent loops where the system reads your git history, loads your project context, and runs until the task is done without you typing a word. Anthropic calls this context engineering — the discipline of designing the entire information environment an agent operates in. The March 2026 source code leak revealed KAIROS, an unreleased always-on daemon mode referenced 150 times in the codebase. When autonomous agents start writing their own prompts, discarding context they deem unimportant, and making decisions while you sleep, the question is not whether this is powerful. The question is who audits the prompts.

ep112-boris-cyrulnik-civilization-resili.title: Boris Cyrulnik on Civilization, Resilience, and Child Development
ep112-boris-cyrulnik-civilization-resili.description:
Boris Cyrulnik, the French neuropsychiatrist who coined the term resilience, delivers a sweeping analysis of modern civilization and its unintended consequences. He draws a key distinction between culture (stable institutions like law, architecture, and marriage) and civilization (the shifting conventions of language, rituals, and social norms). The first 1,000 days of a child's life fundamentally structure temperament — modern neuroimaging shows that sensory and verbal deprivation in infants causes measurable prefrontal lobe atrophy, particularly in boys, crippling their ability to regulate impulses. Every civilizational advance carries secondary effects: screens multiply depression risk fourfold, scheduled C-sections deny babies beneficial microbiome exposure, and women's liberation paradoxically dissolves the family structures that once provided stability. Cyrulnik warns of an empathy crisis driven by personal-development culture's egocentrism and proposes art, literature, and Finnish-style education reform as antidotes. A profound meditation on what we gain and what we lose with every step forward.

ep113-ai-layoff-trap-when-rational-autom.title: The AI Layoff Trap: When Rational Automation Destroys Its Own Market
ep113-ai-layoff-trap-when-rational-autom.description:
Two economists from Wharton and Boston University published a 53-page game-theoretic proof that competitive firms will automate their workforce beyond what is collectively optimal, creating a deadweight loss that harms both workers and firm owners. Brett Hemenway Falk and Gerry Tsoukalas show that when a firm replaces workers with AI, it pockets the cost saving but only bears a fraction of the demand destruction — the rest lands on competitors. The resulting Prisoner's Dilemma means no firm can afford to hold back even though all firms end up worse off. Block cut nearly half its 10,000-person workforce. Salesforce replaced 4,000 agents with AI. Over 100,000 tech workers were laid off in 2025 with AI as a primary driver. The paper evaluates six policy instruments — upskilling, UBI, capital taxes, worker equity, Coasian bargaining, and a Pigouvian automation tax — and finds only the last one fully corrects the distortion. A follow-up paper on SSRN proposes a mesh economy counter-thesis but the original authors already anticipated the gap: every historical displacement episode has left workers with persistent earnings losses. The consent problem is structural: workers did not consent to being laid off, and the market does not self-correct because no individual actor has the incentive to stop.

ep114-ai-made-us-faster-that-was-problem.title: AI Made Us Faster. That Was the Problem
ep114-ai-made-us-faster-that-was-problem.description:
David Fowler, a distinguished engineer at Microsoft leading the .NET Aspire team, published the most honest account yet of what AI-first engineering looks like inside a production team. His team produced what felt like six months of code in one week — and he calls it an overconfidence problem. Production got cheaper but maintenance did not. The bottleneck moved from production capacity to judgment capacity. Experienced engineers feel regression when adopting AI agents, not because the tools are bad but because rebuilding your workflow around a new toolchain feels like putting training wheels back on. Fowler introduces the concept of agent-readiness as codebase health: agents work best with clear structure, good tests, and enough context to verify their own work. Without breakthroughs in memory and continuity, human operators still carry the accumulated product context, architectural intent, and team tradeoffs. AI accelerates the work. Engineers still own the result.

ep115-claude-code-session-management-1m-.title: Claude Code Session Management: A Clean Context Beats a Long Context
ep115-claude-code-session-management-1m-.description:
Thariq Shihipar from Anthropic's Claude Code team published the definitive guide to session management with a 1 million token context window — and the core insight is counterintuitive: having more context does not mean you should use it. Context rot starts degrading model performance well before you hit the limit, with accuracy dropping at just 25 percent of the window. The playbook gives you five moves after every turn: continue, rewind with Esc Esc to drop failed attempts, compact with a hint to shed weight mid-task, clear for a fresh session, and subagents for isolated work that only returns conclusions. The rewind habit is described as the number one pro move: instead of correcting a failed approach, jump back to before it happened and redirect with what you learned. Compact proactively at 50 percent, not reactively at 90, because the model is at its least intelligent when autocompact fires under a bloated context. Subagents are the most underrated tool: they get their own clean context window, do all the messy exploration, and only send back the final result. A clean context beats a long context every time.

ep116-zero-trust-ai-agents-anthropic-sec.title: Zero Trust for AI Agents — Anthropic Security Framework
ep116-zero-trust-ai-agents-anthropic-sec.description:
Anthropic published a 35-page security framework in May 2026 that applies Zero Trust principles to autonomous AI agents in the enterprise. The premise is blunt: perimeter-based security is dead, AI models have compressed exploit timelines from months to hours, and agents make every existing access control model look like a suggestion. The framework introduces least agency — a term from OWASP extending least privilege to restrict what each agent tool can do, how often, and where. It maps controls across three tiers (Foundation, Enterprise, Advanced) covering agent identity, access control, resource isolation, observability, behavioral monitoring, input validation, integrity, and recovery. The Foundation floor has been raised: static API keys are treated as already compromised, short-lived tokens and cryptographic identity are entry requirements. The threat landscape covers prompt injection, tool poisoning via MCP servers, tool chaining attacks, memory poisoning, and supply chain risks including malicious models. Implementation follows eight phases from requirements through supply chain management to defensive operations. Anthropic closes with Agentic SOAR — AI agents handling evidence collection and documentation while humans stay on containment decisions. The uncomfortable question the framework raises but does not answer: who sets the trust boundaries when agents decide how to interpret your instructions?

ep117-openhands-open-source-ai-software-.title: OpenHands — Open Source AI Software Engineer
ep117-openhands-open-source-ai-software-.description:
OpenHands, originally called OpenDevin, launched from Carnegie Mellon research and has accumulated 75,000 GitHub stars, raised 18.8 million dollars, and become the open-source answer to autonomous coding agents. Unlike autocomplete tools, OpenHands runs agents that plan, act, observe, and reflect in a loop inside sandboxed Docker containers with real code editors, shells, browsers, and task planners. The Software Agent SDK is a composable Python framework that separates model intelligence from agent capability, letting you swap Claude for GPT for Llama without rewriting agent logic. Use cases include vulnerability remediation, COBOL-to-Java migration, incident triage, and PR review. The OpenHands Index, launched January 2026, is the first broad-coverage benchmark for agentic software engineering, revealing that context management is the key differentiator, not raw model size. Enterprise deployment runs on-premise or air-gapped with full audit trails. An AMD partnership brings local inference on Ryzen AI hardware. The honest limit: OpenHands excels at well-scoped, verifiable tasks and struggles with ambiguous requirements and deep domain knowledge. The community recommendation is autonomous agents for 80 percent of backend work, interactive IDE tools for debugging and refinement.

ep118-liberland-2026-master-plan.title: Liberland 2026 Master Plan
ep118-liberland-2026-master-plan.description:
Vít Jedlička delivered his 2026 New Year address with a concrete forty million dollar investment plan for the Baranja region surrounding Liberland. The speech covered three strategic pillars. First, legitimacy through citizens in power: Javier Milei governing Argentina, Peter Mitsinka as Czech Foreign Minister, and Somaliland gaining recognition after being first to recognize Liberland in 2017. Second, blockchain governance infrastructure: Justin Sun re-elected as Prime Minister, bringing Tron ecosystem resources, with 2026 priorities on blockchain bridges to centralized financial systems and DAO-based company registration. Third, financial services: Liberland Bank and Liberland Pay launching as centralized banking complements to the decentralized governance layer. The citizenship target is one million applicants. The budget is projected to double. The dual architecture — decentralized governance with centralized financial plumbing — mirrors the same pattern successful crypto exchanges use, applied to a nation-state with territorial sovereignty as its regulatory advantage. Whether Serbia and Croatia accept the economic partnership offer for Baranja is the open question.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberland
https://liberland.org/en/
